text:
marta: FYI escalation from Acme — they saw intermittent 500s on our /v1/embeddings endpoint yesterday evening. customer provided a request_id: req_0a1b2c3d4e and a curl repro. Can someone try lookup in server logs?
sam: dropping the request_id here, thanks. do we have retention windows for prod logs? iirc it's 14 days for app-logs but edge/gateway might be longer.
logs-bot: automated search started for request_id=req_0a1b2c3d4e across indices: prod-app-*, prod-edge-* (time range: 2026-02-25..2026-03-16).
logs-bot: search result: 0 hits in prod-app-* (index retention 14d). request timestamp in customer's report is 2026-02-24T21:41:02Z — outside app-logs retention window.
ingrid: if app logs are evicted we can try edge/gateway (rotating logs kept 30d) or s3 archived logs. try this Loki query against edge cluster (approx):
```
{job="edge-gateway"} |= "req_0a1b2c3d4e" | json | line_format "{ts} {level} {msg}"
```
raj: also try searching by client_ip or by the upstream target name (embed-service-v2). sometimes request_id isn't persisted end-to-end. ask customer for the curl they ran (headers) and the client IP/time window.
marta: their curl (redacted token) was:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-client-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello world"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/embeddings"
```
sam: ok — ask them to re-run with an X-Debug-Token header we can use to correlate if logs are evicted, e.g. set X-Debug-Token: acme-20260315-1 and include --compressed if they used compression. Also request the full debug bundle (curl + response + local timestamps).
marta: sending instructions now. message to customer: "Could you rerun the call with a unique X-Debug-Token header and include the exact request timestamp, client IP, and the raw response body? If possible, add --header 'X-Debug-Token: acme-20260315-1' so our side can correlate edge logs."
raj: if they can’t reproduce, ask for a tcpdump or client-side HAR and we can run a fingerprint search in archived s3 logs. snippet for kibana filter i’ll run if we get a time window:
```
@timestamp >= "2026-02-24T21:30:00Z" AND @timestamp <= "2026-02-24T21:50:00Z" AND (http.status_code:500 OR http.response.keyword: "upstream_timeout")
```
logs-bot: quick telemetry check: found 3x 500s in edge-gateway for embed-service-v2 between 2026-02-24T21:37..21:45Z showing upstream timeout to embed-worker-12. Full trace ids: trace-a1b2, trace-c3d4, trace-e5f6 (edge logs only).
sam: nice find — edge has traces even if app logs are gone. can we fetch those traces and see upstream latency?
ingrid: grabbing traces now. early signs point to sporadic connection resets from embed-worker-12; i'll escalate to infra to check node health and recent restarts.
marta: thanks all. I'll update Acme: asking them to rerun with X-Debug-Token and to send debug bundle; telling them we located edge traces and infra is investigating an upstream worker. :thumbsup:
sam: once we have the debug bundle / new req id i'll run the cross-index search and hand off to eng-sre for root cause. :eyes:
raj: if we confirm worker flapping we may need to remove embed-worker-12 from rotation and roll a patched image. i'll stand by.
marta: closing loop with customer now, will post updates in this thread.
